mechanism_verified_statically: Every FileSecretStore directory operation validates the private directory and takes flock on that opened directory inode; all cooperating initialize/put/read/recover calls share the lock. Acquisition uses a one-second monotonic bound; process exit closes/releases the kernel lock.

Recovery admits only reserved .staging-32hex names and requires no-follow regular current-user exact-0600 bounded files. Link count must be one or two; two requires exactly one named immutable secret or fingerprint destination in the same directory with identical device/inode.

The whole staging candidate set is validated before deletion, and inode identity is checked again before unlink. Recovery removes staging names only; a linked immutable destination is preserved with its original bytes.

Initialize recovers interrupted staging before validating an existing fingerprint key. Cleanup validates all committed provider configuration reference chains under the database writer transaction before stage recovery and deletion of truly unreferenced immutable versions.

Save-secret writes physical versions inside the database writer transaction. This keeps service-level CAS writers excluded while cleanup calculates retained references; the storage lock additionally prevents cleanup from deleting a concurrently active staged write.
Other five original production/migration inputs have identical bytes to the complete original static review; ACK, terminal and backup code did not change for this repair.
tests_reviewed_for_meaning: Two real child os._exit seams leave actual pre-link nlink1 and post-link nlink2 filesystem states. Original logs fail on leftover stage/unavailable deletion, then the same five-case test file passes after the production repair.

Three controlled concurrent operations (cleanup, initialize, put) actually wait while a child holds its staged write, then complete after release. The 150ms observation is a scheduling test, not a universal throughput or latency guarantee.

Two added real initialization crash seams verify recovery and preservation of an already linked fingerprint key. Seven unsafe-entry cases cover symlink/directory/FIFO/mode/external hardlink/three links/oversize, preserving the entire candidate set on initial validation failure.

Existing configuration integration tests verify committed and historical versions survive orphan cleanup and committed-reference corruption fails before deletion. Post-link crashed newly allocated secret in the real seam is uncommitted because put has not returned; it is correctly reclaimed as an orphan.
remaining_scope_limits: Reviewer performed static reads, hash comparisons and readback of owner-generated original receipts/logs only; did not rerun any test, browser, network request or credential access.

File fallback was exercised on the current local POSIX/Linux environment. No actual OS-backed SecretStore, Windows portability, remote provider, real key or complete M5.1 platform acceptance is established.

flock serializes cooperating FileSecretStore clients. It is not a guarantee against hostile same-user processes bypassing the store or replacing the private directory, and does not promise physical byte erasure.
The original red/green full test file hash is equal in both original receipts; this addendum archives only the actual current expanded test source, not a reconstruction of the earlier test file.

Final50 result is an owner development run on the listed immutable source hashes; independent reviewer did not review every body in all five final test modules or promote it to a fixed-commit full-suite result.
